svg.title: RPE computation showing surprise not magnitude
svg.desc: RPE equals actual minus predicted. Four examples show that high magnitude outcomes produce low RPE if expected, while low magnitude outcomes produce high RPE if surprising. This property ensures learning updates world model not just outcome preference.

g.text: both expressed as normalized value in same units (e.g. pressure relief score 0–1)
positive RPE = better than expected · negative RPE = worse than expected · zero = exactly as expected

svg.text: four cases · same action · different prediction accuracy

g.text: case A vs case D: both got good outcomes, but A expected good while D expected bad.
RPE correctly signals "learn more from D" — it revealed a wrong prediction about the world.
if RPE encoded magnitude instead, A and D would get similar updates — but A taught nothing
new. RPE encodes the gap in the world model, which is exactly what needs to be corrected.
